atlas-bg.0127: Register as a job-seeker at the employment agency within seven working days of graduating, and apply to the Migration Directorate at least 30 days before your student permit ends.
atlas-bg.0128: A contract of at least six months and a three-year degree, or for IT three years of experience in the last seven; no labour-market test. The card lasts two to five years; after 12 months you can change employer by notice, and family can join at once with the right to work.
atlas-bg.0131: The employer applies while you are abroad, after advertising the job for 15 days with the employment agency, and non-EU staff may be at most 20% of the workforce (35% in small firms). The permit is tied to that employer and job.
atlas-bg.0132: A hosting agreement with a research body registered with NACID; research and teaching with no work permit, and family reunion at once.
atlas-bg.0133: Doctoral scholarships are free of income tax and social contributions.
atlas-bg.0134: Bulgaria has no working-holiday or youth-mobility agreement with any country; the only seasonal route is a permit for farm and tourism work of 90 days to 9 months.
atlas-bg.0135: Bulgaria is fully in Schengen since 1 January 2025: days here count in the same 90 in any 180, with no work. A tourist or visa-free stay cannot be converted inside Bulgaria.
atlas-bg.0136: Nothing to arrange in advance: you may stay up to 3 months freely, with no visa or work authorisation.
atlas-bg.0137: Apply for the D visa at the Bulgarian consulate where you live: €100.
atlas-bg.0138: Staying over 3 months, register within 3 months at the regional Migration Directorate, with ID, a work contract registered with the revenue agency (or your employer’s statement) and proof of housing. Students bring their enrolment certificate, European Health Insurance Card and a statement that they support themselves.
atlas-bg.0139: Register your address within 3 calendar days of entering. In private rented housing this needs the owner’s notarised declaration of accommodation and a copy of the title deed.
atlas-bg.0140: The paper long-stay certificate is issued the same day, for €3.58 (7 BGN).
atlas-bg.0141: The biometric residence card costs €20.45 (40 BGN), on top of the fee for the permit itself.
atlas-bg.0142: The Interior Ministry assigns a 10-digit personal number for foreigners (LNCh) with your first long-stay residence document; the personal number EGN is only for Bulgarians and permanent or long-term residents.
atlas-bg.0143: Before you have it, the National Revenue Agency can issue a service number for tax, banking or company paperwork.
atlas-bg.0144: Employees are enrolled in the public health fund (NHIF) through their pay: 8% of gross, 4.8% paid by the employer and 3.2% by you.
atlas-bg.0145: Students and others not working are covered by their European Health Insurance Card, which they show when registering.
atlas-bg.0146: Students, interns, funded researchers and family members need private health insurance from an authorised insurer, covering at least €30,000 (60,000 BGN) for emergency care and repatriation.
atlas-bg.0147: Legal residents have a right to a basic account, but banks (UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, UBB, Fibank) in practice want you in person with your personal number card, and may charge non-residents for identity checks.
atlas-bg.0148: Applying for or renewing a permit gets you a receipt with a filing number: it keeps you legal in Bulgaria and, on a renewal, lets you keep working for the same employer, but it is valid only inside Bulgaria.
atlas-bg.0149: If your D visa has expired and the card is not ready, do not travel to or through other Schengen countries; only a direct flight home is safe.
atlas-bg.0150: Apply for the permit at least 14 days before your D visa expires; later, the application is rejected and you are unlawfully present.
atlas-bg.0151: Register your address within three days of arriving; in a private rental you need the owner’s notarised declaration and title deed.
atlas-bg.0152: Foreign criminal records expire six months after issue and must be translated by translators authorised by the Bulgarian foreign ministry.
atlas-bg.0153: The application receipt is valid only inside Bulgaria: with an expired D visa, only a direct flight home is possible.
atlas-bg.0154: Since the euro, state fees are being re-set: the EU registration certificate is reported at €7 (paper) or €18 (card), and other fees still need re-reading.
atlas-bg.0155: A draft would raise the D visa fee from €100 to €120.
atlas-bg.0156: Whether the 20% foreign-staff cap applies to Blue Card hires in start-ups is not settled.
atlas-bg.0157: Banks still make it hard for non-residents to open an account.
